items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Benny was the guy who showed me -- the first -- the first guy that showed me how to take care of a slide.

ctx.x: caring for slides and things in those days. In fact, I was talking out to the factory here today -- the other day -- Olds Factory.

There was a little guy who worked out there named Benny years ago. He was crippled. That's when Olds Factory was -- this was '32, somewhere around that time. It was on Raymond Street. And he knew so much about slides. He worked on horns. I was talkin to He's dead now. The top machinist -- one of the top machinists out at Olds Factory now And he said Benny taught him. And he said, yeah, I remember Benny. Benny was the guy who taught me. I said, well, Benny was the guy who showed me -- the first -- the first guy…

I didn't -- I just played. I didn't know anything about taking care of the thing or anything. I just played it and that was it. When we came up we didn't -- you know, we didn't know anything about things like that. So, I teach kids today about horns. And the average kid playing the horn, they don't know really the proper care for a horn, how You should keep the horn clean and -- because I didn't know it. I try to help kids today.
